summary.headline: H1 FY27 PAT rose 92% YoY to ₹52 crore on operating revenue up 25% to ₹1,329 crore; trailing FCF ₹204 crore.
summary.overview: Renaissance Global reported Q2 FY27 operating revenue up 20% YoY to ₹639 crore and H1 operating revenue up 25% to ₹1,329 crore (excluding bullion). H1 EBITDA rose 21% to ₹101 crore at a 7.6% margin, while PAT nearly doubled to ₹52 crore. Operating cash flow turned positive at ₹143 crore in H1 versus an outflow of ₹83 crore a year earlier, and net debt fell 42% YoY to ₹199 crore. Management is exiting consignment-heavy customer-brand accounts (about ₹400 crore of revenue) to cut working capital, which is diluting near-term gross margin.

segments.name: Jean-Ducet (own brand, luxury lab-grown diamonds)
segments.commentary: Four boutiques operating (LA, New York, San Francisco, Boston; Boston opened 4 Nov 2026); four more planned in Washington DC, Chicago, Miami, Dallas to reach eight by end FY27. Own-brand revenue grew over 50% in the quarter per management; FY27 Jean-Ducet revenue guided at ₹160-175 crore. Gross margin ~68%, four-wall contribution ~43%, store payback 12-15 months.

segments.name: With Clarity (digital-first fine jewelry)
segments.commentary: Growing in the mid-20s% YoY; FY27 expected revenue ~₹220 crore. Gross margin ~63%, marketplace model for certified lab diamonds with in-house design and manufacturing of the metal.

segments.name: Own brands combined
segments.commentary: Own brands (Jean-Ducet + With Clarity) grew 39% in Q2; expected FY27 revenue ₹375 crore, of which ₹172 crore achieved in H1. Brand CAGR of 66% since FY22.

segments.name: Customer brands (B2B, incl. consignment)
segments.commentary: Exiting customers with ~₹400 crore annual revenue due to long working-capital cycles. FY27 segment revenue expected ~₹1,700-1,800 crore; run-rate next year ~₹1,400-1,500 crore. Segment margin guided at 6-8%.

segments.name: Licensed brands (House of Disney)
segments.commentary: Retained as a pillar of the branded portfolio; management aims to focus on globally recognised franchises. No separate financials disclosed in the call.

guidance_outlook: Build a ₹1,000 crore D2C business by FY29 through own brands, store expansion, digital and operating leverage.
Jean-Ducet network to reach eight boutiques by end FY27; new stores target ~₹25-30 crore annual sales each (new US stores assumed ~$2.5 million).
Working capital cycle target ~180 days; net debt target ~₹100 crore by 2030.
Exit of customers with ~₹400 crore revenue run-rate to complete by end FY27; H2 margins expected to improve on seasonality and mix.
Customer brands margin expected to stay in 6-8% range with lower working-capital intensity; overall company margin to rise on mix shift.
capex_capacity: Boutique capex plus inventory about ₹10-12 crore per store.
Only ~25% of products sold are manufactured in-house; Jean-Ducet manufacturing to move in-house over 12-18 months, constrained by Baal Nagar facility shutdown and skill-set training.
Cash and investments of about ₹383 crore held partly for acquisitions; management says ongoing acquisition conversations exist, no details shared.
demand_pricing: Jean-Ducet average order value about $5,500 (store ~$7,500, online ~$4,500); made-to-order is about 50% of business, delivered in 3-4 weeks.
Legacy Jean-Ducet stores (New York, LA) growing high single digit same-store sales, mainly volume; prices stable. New York first-year sales above ₹30 crore; San Francisco tracking to ₹25-30 crore.
Competition: Brilliant Earth, Blue Nile in lab-grown digital; management sees luxury lab-grown white space with no direct luxury competitor. With Clarity is much smaller than peers.
Rupee about 10-15% weaker YoY, supporting rupee revenue from dollar-denominated sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why are forex losses recurring when most sales are exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Dollar-denominated borrowings (about ₹550-600 crore gross, majority of debt) are revalued on rupee depreciation, driving forex losses. Management suggested analysts judge gross margin after forex adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost up and contract manufacturing up?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost reduction of about ₹40-50 crore (all overheads, ~₹40 crore in FY26) cut headcount. Trade goods rose due to Jean-Ducet sourcing and capacity constraints after Baal Nagar shutdown; only ~25% of sales are self-manufactured now.

qa_highlights.question: Has working capital been released as previously communicated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan stands: over 12 months, ₹550 crore incremental revenue was added with about ₹417 crore less working capital than at the old intensity; CFO of ₹280 crore funded debt reduction. Net working capital in absolute terms was not reduced.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross debt not reduced despite strong cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of debt is about 6-7%; ₹383 crore cash is held for acquisition optionality and next-year needs, following the playbook of acquire, turn around, scale.

qa_highlights.question: Store unit economics and payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin 68%, operating overhead ~25% of sales, giving ~43% four-wall contribution before national advertising. Payback 12-15 months. Marketing ~25% of sales in FY26 falling to 17-18% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the consignment share of customer brands 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not believe it was 50%; exits are 100%-consignment accounts; exact share to be provided later. Inventory is 30-50% consignment per management.

risks_watch: Gross margin dilution from selling down inventory with exited customers; H1 ex-bullion margin 7.6% vs 7.9% a year earlier.
Recurring forex losses from ~$550-600 crore dollar borrowings; forex treatment and presentation may be revisited.
Accounting methodology for bullion sales expected to change in FY28; bullion sales of ₹146 crore in H1 are currently not core.
Store ramp risk: new boutiques take 14-25 weeks to mature; monitor 25 appointments/week KPI for new stores.
Rising trade-goods share and reliance on outsourcing; Jean-Ducet in-house manufacturing transition expected over 12-18 months.
Unannounced acquisitions could absorb ₹383 crore cash and delay deleveraging.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Jean-Ducet store economics and cash flow, but defensive on margin dilution, forex losses and some accounting/working-capital questions, deferring details to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: We are pleased to have delivered a strong performance during the first half of FY27 with operating revenues growing 25% year over year while profit after tax grew almost 90% year over year.
Our net debt has declined to 199 crores as of September 2026 marking its lowest level in recent years.

So, in effect, we've saved 417 crores of working capital because had the business been at the same working capital intensity would have needed far more capital than we did, then we actually needed to needed to use.
